'''Hungarian''' '''cuisine''' ([[Hungarian language|Hungarian]]: ''magyar konyhaművészet'') is the [[cuisine]] characteristic of the nation of [[Hungary]], and its primary ethnic group, [[Hungarians]]. Hungarian cuisine has been described as being the [[Pungency|spiciest]] cuisine in [[Europe]].<ref>{{Cite web |first=Alona |last=Tiunina |date=2022-09-11 |title=5 European Countries For Foodies |url=https://www.jetsettogether.com/5-european-countries-for-foodies/ |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Jet Set Together |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bociąga |first=Przemysław |date=2023-03-19 |title=Hungary is the Central European Capital of Chili Peppers |url=https://3seaseurope.com/paprika-chili-peppers-hungary/ |access-date=2023-07-05 |website=3 Seas Europe |language=en-US}}</ref> This can largely be attributed to the use of their piquant native spice, [[Paprika#Hungarian|Hungarian paprika]], in many of their dishes. A mild version of the spice, Hungarian sweet paprika, is commonly used as an alternative.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Emily |last=Han  |date=April 4, 2022 |title=Different Types of Paprika, Explained |url=https://www.thekitchn.com/whats-the-difference-hot-sweet-68134 |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Kitchn |language=en}}</ref> Traditional Hungarian dishes are primarily based on meats, seasonal vegetables, fruits, bread, and dairy products.
